sections.heading: Ai nên hành động hoặc chờ

Để tài sản thế chấp này tin cậy với ngân hàng, không cần thẩm định viên đến tận nơi để xem xét, Cowmed trang bị cho mỗi con bò một vòng cổ thông minh Smarty Collar sử dụng trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI). Với người đọc, khung hữu ích gồm bằng chứng hiện có, nhóm bị ảnh hưởng, rủi ro còn lại và điểm nên kiểm tra trước khi hành động. Phần này cần gọi đúng nhóm độc giả nên hành động ngay hoặc nên chờ thêm xác nhận.

sections.heading: Điều cần theo dõi tiếp
sections.body: Vòng cổ này liên tục ghi lại tình trạng sức khỏe, hành vi và vị trí của bò. Dữ liệu thô sau đó được chuyển thành định danh kỹ thuật số được mã hóa, liên kết trực tiếp với thỏa thuận tín dụng B3. Một bài tốt cần tách rõ sự kiện từ nguồn, tác động với người đọc và câu hỏi theo dõi để không giống bản tóm tắt link rời. draft_context.source_title: Apple Upgrade Program Will Let You Lease an iPhone Without Sticker Shock
draft_context.description: The program will take the sting out of owning Apple devices, including Macs, iPads and Apple Watches.
paragraphs: There’s now a new way to own an Apple product. Starting from today in the US, you’ll be able to lease an iPhone, iPad, Mac or Apple Watch directly from the company via its new Apple Upgrad e program.

Enabled by Klarna, prices for leasing Apple products will start at $18 a month for an iPhone and $12 a month for an Apple Watch , with 12- and 24-month leasing options. If you’re in the market for an iPad or Mac , you’re likely to keep that device for longer, and Apple is offering 24- or 36-month leasing options for these devices.

You can explore the different options either online or through the Apple Store, or you can go to a physical Apple Store in person. If you have an existing device to trade in, you can also lower your monthly leasing costs.

The leasing program is likely to come as welcome news to anyone overwhelmed by the thought of buying an Apple device outright — especially right now. Just last month, Apple abruptly raised prices of all of its devices due to RAMageddon , the industry-wide memory shortage that’s pushing up prices not just of Apple products, but all consumer electronics. This came shortly after Apple CEO Tim Cook called price rises “unavoidable.”

The price rises are also expected to affect upcoming launches, including at Apple’s rumored September iPhone event. If Apple does unveil a new foldable iPhone, as expected, it’s likely to be more expensive than any existing models, just as Samsung’s foldables are more expensive than its other flagship phones.

A leasing program could well prove a popular strategy at a time when many households are struggling with the cost of living. It’s a major financial challenge for Apple to balance rising component costs at a time when people are only becoming more price sensitive, said Dipanjan Chatterjee, vice president and chief analyst at Forrester.

draft_context.source_title: It seems like every OS update is loaded with security fixes–here’s why
draft_context.description: Macworld It used to be that operating system “point releases”—the minor updates throughout the year—contained around a dozen security vulnerability fixes. But that number has been growing in the last couple of years and has exploded in the past few months. There were 35 security vulnerabilities fixed in iOS 26.4. That went up to 43 in iOS 26.5. A 26.5.2 update solely for security fixes added another 29. There are an unprecedented 77 security vulnerabilities fixed in iOS and iPadOS 26.6 . Think that’s a lot? The macOS 26.6 update has almost twice as many, with 142 fixes on Apple’s Security Updates page . Thanks to AI coding agents, this is the new normal. You can expect dozens of security vulnerabilities to be fixed every couple of months, at least for a while. Why is this happening? You can thank, and blame, AI for this. AI coding agents have gotten good. Very good. Not only has “vibe coding” become commonplace, but the best AI models can analyze and test very large code blocks and databases. And they find things that people miss. A few months ago, we wrote about Project Glasswing , a collaboration between Anthropic and a handful of other companies (including Apple) to provide those companies’ security researchers with access to the company’s most advanced AI model, in the hopes of finding vulnerabilities before the models become public and all the bad actors get their hands on them. The world we live in right now is one of security acceleration. Hackers and malicious groups can use advanced AI tools to find unique vulnerabilities that can, sometimes in combination with each other, compromise systems like never before. The sort of resources and research once only available to nation-states and the largest tech corporations are now broadly available. But AI is having just as much of an impact on the positive side. Security researchers are using these tools to find more vulnerabilities than ever, reporting them to software companies, who now, thanks to AI coding tools, have the scope to address more of them more quickly. For the time being, we’re in an AI-accelerated arms race between the hackers who use AI to find vulnerabilities and exploit them, and the researchers and developers who use AI to find vulnerabilities and fix or report them. And it’s resulting in increasingly large and important security update releases. This may eventually wind down, as the AI coding tools get sophisticated and commonplace enough to more thoroughly test massive code databases and all their interactions with other code before its ever released. But for the time being, and likely for some time to come, expect operating system updates—including Apple’s—to fix a big list of security issues with every release.

There were 35 security vulnerabilities fixed in iOS 26.4. That went up to 43 in iOS 26.5. A 26.5.2 update solely for security fixes added another 29.

There are an unprecedented 77 security vulnerabilities fixed in iOS and iPadOS 26.6 . Think that’s a lot? The macOS 26.6 update has almost twice as many, with 142 fixes on Apple’s Security Updates page .
Thanks to AI coding agents, this is the new normal. You can expect dozens of security vulnerabilities to be fixed every couple of months, at least for a while.
